answer:
**ICAV vs. Irish investment plc**

| Feature | ICAV (ICAV Act 2015) | Investment plc (Companies Act 2014, Part 24) |
|---|---|---|
| **Sub-fund accounts** | An umbrella may prepare separate financial statements for each sub-fund. | Umbrella-level accounts only. Sub-fund figures are included, but standalone statements aren't permitted. |
| **AGMs** | The board may dispense with AGMs by notice. Shareholders or the auditor can still require one. | Generally mandatory. Dispensing requires unanimous written shareholder consent, which is impractical for listed ETFs. |
| **US tax** | Not a "per se corporation," so it can check-the-box to be a partnership or disregarded entity. This is often done per sub-fund, avoiding PFIC treatment for US investors. | On the per se corporation list, so it is always a corporation and cannot elect. |

This flexibility is why most new Irish ETF umbrellas are ICAVs.

**ICAV vs. Irish investment plc**

| Feature | ICAV (ICAV Act 2015) | Investment plc (Companies Act 2014, Part 24) |
|---|---|---|
| **Per-sub-fund accounts** | An umbrella ICAV may prepare separate financial statements for each sub-fund. | Accounts must be prepared for the umbrella company as a whole. Sub-fund figures appear within them, but standalone statements aren't permitted. |
| **AGMs** | The board can dispense with AGMs by giving shareholders notice. Shareholders, or the auditor, can still require one. | AGMs are generally mandatory. Dispensing with one requires unanimous written shareholder consent, which is impractical for a listed ETF. |
| **US tax classification** | Not a "per se corporation" under US Treasury regulations, so it can make a check-the-box election to be treated as a partnership or disregarded entity. In practice this is often done sub-fund by sub-fund, which avoids PFIC treatment for US investors. | An Irish plc is on the per se corporation list, so it is always treated as a corporation and cannot elect. |

This flexibility is why most new Irish ETF umbrellas use the ICAV form.
